statement.p: Let (x_0, y_0) = (1, 3) and (x_1, y_1) = (1.5, 3.3). Use the following graph of the function f to find the indicated derivatives.

image.shortdescription: Graph of a function and its tangent line at a point.

description.p: graph of a function passing through the point (x_0,y_0) and the line tangent to the function at (x_0,y_0) which also passes through the point (x_1,y_1)

solution.p: Since the point (1,3) is on the curve, we know f(1)=3. The point (1.5,3.3) is on the tangent line, so \hbox{Slope of tangent} = \frac{3.3-3}{1.5-1} = \frac{0.3}{0.5} = 0.6. Thus, f'(1)=0.6.
By the chain rule h'(1) = 3(f(1))^{2}\cdot f'(1) =3\cdot 3^{2}\cdot 0.6 = 16.2.

Because g(x) is the inverse function of f, we know that g(3) = 1. Then note that f(g(x)) = f(f^{-1}(x)) = x, so f(g(x)) = x. Differentiating both sides of the equation, f'(g(x))\cdot g'(x) = 1, so g'(x) = \frac{1}{f'(g(x))}. Thus g'(3) = \frac{1}{f'(g(3))} = \frac{1}{f'(1)} = \frac1{0.6}.
